# `get_verify_str`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Fetch a fresh per-socket challenge string for client verification.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, preprocessClientAuth @0x6b6bb0, cli_verify_get_randstr @0x6b2550 (64-bit imager build); 32-bit preprocessClientAuth @0x6814d8; app 3.3.2 VerifyAction and GetVerifyStrCmd |

First step of client verification. Matched by the authentication preprocessor before any method table, so it is answered even on an unverified external connection (and is not one of the main-table names). Params are ignored. The device generates a fresh 32-character challenge, stores it for this socket (replacing any earlier one) and returns it as result.str with code 0. It does not clear an existing verified flag. The challenge is valid only on the socket that fetched it. Only single requests get this dedicated reply; inside a batch from an unverified client the whole batch is consumed silently. The app treats code 103 on its first get_verify_str as a legacy device without verification and continues; any other failure ends its session. Ports with this preprocessor: 4700, 4701, 4702, 4400 and 4040. Verification on 4040 also gates the 4030 serial bridge by source IP (ports.md R3a).

Side effects: Replaces this socket's stored challenge (connection-local state). No device setting or hardware state changes. Tier B is INFERRED (per-socket session bookkeeping only); no tier was graded for the authentication preprocessor, and tier A is excluded because the challenge store is a shared session write.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_verify_str"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Ignored. The app sends no params member. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Request has no id; reply has id null and no method member | `invalid id` |

No handler error is established. Invalid JSON gets the ordinary 101 parse-error reply. Code 103 is not sent by a build with this preprocessor; the app treats 103 on its first get_verify_str as a legacy device without verification.

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":1,"method":"get_verify_str"}
```

Reply, ok - Challenge value is a placeholder of the right length, not a captured value:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_verify_str","result":{"str":"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdef"},"code":0,"id":1}
```

Reply, no-id:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","error":"invalid id","code":200,"id":null}
```
